model.architecture: Jan-nano is a 4B deep-research agent fine-tuned from Qwen3-4B (Qwen3ForCausalLM) with a multi-stage RLVR recipe, optimized for tool use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

variants.quantization: int4 block 128 weights (symmetric) + OCTAV optimal-clipping; embeddings INT8 (externalized section); KV cache 4096

recommended.reason: the Android path verified on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24): full delegation (3270 ops across 2 subgraphs) and a correct answer to the probe; 9.7 tok/s decode, engine init 6.2 s, peak 1021 MB. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is the verified choice for the class, not a measured win over CPU; the repo's model_block32.litertlm decodes 9.37 tok/s on the same device and backend, so this file carries the class

platform_notes: Reasoning model: run with max_tokens ≥ 2048 — at a short limit it gets cut off mid-thought and never reaches the answer (all quality numbers measured at 2048).
Google AI Edge Gallery v1.0.16+ can import litert-lm models directly from Hugging Face inside the app (tap +); manual adb steps only for older builds or sideloading.
A 4B int4 build needs ~2.5 GB free RAM on the phone; reboot first if memory is tight.
Galaxy S26: XNNPACK additionally takes 1 of the 4 nodes in decode_embedder and prefill_embedder_128; the runtime accepts that split.
Reproducibility: GPU rows repeat to within ~1%; CPU rows are noisier (treat the CPU column as accurate to roughly ±7%).
Recommended file: use model.litertlm (block 128) — ~40% faster decode than block 32 while matching it on accuracy here, and the build that loads reliably on iPhone.
The desktop (M4 Max) rows are this file; the iPhone row is carried over from an earlier on-device note whose run log is not retained (run count and prompt unknown).

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); same-device control for an existing GPU row on this handset

known_issues: At a short max_tokens the model is cut off mid-<think> and never reaches the answer; needs max_tokens ≥ 2048.
iPhone: the block-32 build's 2.11 GiB section sits at the device memory ceiling and may fail to load — prefer block 128 on iPhone.
At max_tokens 1024 the block-32 build scored only 63% on GSM8K because its longer int4 reasoning chains were truncated before the answer; at 2048 it recovers to 85% (−7 pt vs bf16).
